svg.title: Strangle payoff at expiration
svg.desc: A long strangle loses money in a flat band between the put and call strikes, and only becomes profitable once the stock moves far enough past either strike to clear both breakeven points. Uses the real MSFT trade's numbers: put strike 355, call strike 435, total cost 30.54 per share.
svg.text: Real example: the MSFT trade — $355 put + $435 call, $30.54/share total cost
put strike - premium, or call strike + premium
Max loss: -$3,054 total (the full premium paid)
The stock has to clear ONE of the two break-evens before expiration for the trade to profit —
landing anywhere between $355 and $435 loses the full premium, no matter which direction it came from.
Every strangle the bot has placed — real Alpaca fills, as of Oct 1, 2026
Stock px = close on the entry day → price when the last leg sold · 1 contract each (×100 shares) · open P&L = sold legs + current value of held legs − cost
Exit rules: before Aug 3 the bot sold each leg on its own once that leg was up 10–15% (“old rule”); since Aug 3 it judges call + put together and closes both at ±20% of total cost.

* The old bot recorded these sales even though the order never filled, so it stopped managing the leg. Re-adopted Oct 1 from Alpaca — most are already past ±20%, so the bot will try to close them on its next run.
Source: Alpaca order fills + positions (prices, dates), strangle_state.json (strikes, expiry, earnings), Alpaca bars (stock price).
